newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's National Mutual ponders more direct services.
newsitem.headline: NZ's National Mutual ponders more direct services.

text.p: National Mutual is considering launching direct sales of products such as term deposits and home mortgages, the New Zealand Herald reported on Wednesday.

National Mutual already has around $300 million worth of those sorts of product. It would differentiate its services from AMP's Ergo direct sales arm by offering only price-driven products not needing specialist advice, the company's New Zealand general manager Ross McEwan said.
However, that should not be taken to indicate a running-down of the advisory support arm.

McEwan said more aggressive promotion of the New Zealand advisory group would be a priority; a useful example was that of National Mutual Financial Planners, which has won accredited adviser status to organisations such as the Australian Council of Trade Unions.
Another initiative would be to gain greater recognition for the "very good and consistent" performance of National Mutual Fund Managers, he said.
McEwan said National Mutual in New Zealand was now taking an outward-looking direction after two years of internal focus on demutualisation and listing.
The emphasis now was on the company's distribution force, "the people who are going to deliver the greatest level of business".

With a strong profile among traditional investment advisers and financial planners, the next move was to build up the distribution of risk, insurance, and retirement savings products through the broker market.
The salaried sales force has risen to about 30 over the past six months, finding a strong market in Auckland and expanding into Christchurch.
McEwan, who replaced former chief Anthony Ractliffe, has spent the past 2 1/2 years at National Mutual's Melbourne head office.
